newsitem.title: BERMUDA: NZ SPORT - England head towards innings win.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - England head towards innings win.

text.p: England were heading towards an emphatic win over Northern Districts on Monday on the third morning of their four-day tour match.
Northern Districts, resuming at 99 for one in their second innings and needing a further 126 to make England bat again, lost both their overnight batsmen inside the first 40 minutes.
Matthew Bell shouldered arms at the fourth ball of the morning from fast-medium Darren Gough and was bowled, without adding to his overnight 35.
With Blair Pocock, he had added 90 for the second wicket to put some substance into the Northern Districts innings.
Pocock, who began on 60, swept offspinner Robert Croft for four, but had added just nine runs today when he shaped to turn Gough towards mid on, missed and was leg before wicket.
He had given himself a good workout leading up to the first test against England, starting in Auckland on Friday. He batted 208 minutes, faced 151 balls and hit nine boundaries.
Gough, who hadn't been called on until the 31st over of the innings, produced his liveliest spell of the tour, taking two for six off seven overs, five of which were maidens.
Michael Parlane and Mark Bailey wasted no time getting their innings' started.
Parlane drove Gough to the point boundary to get off the mark, then Bailey lofted Croft back down the ground for six.
After an hour's play today, Northern Districts had moved to 127 for three, with Bailey on 12 and Parlane on six.
